mode.title: Estimate mode
mode.ballparkHelp: A preliminary Low / Expected / High range from the guided interview, shared geometry and explicit assumptions. Line-by-line pricing is not required.
mode.detailedHelp: Line-level pricing with exception handling. Every line needs a quantity and a price.
mode.exceptionsOptional: Optional — unresolved lines widen the range instead of blocking it.

switched.ballpark: Switched to Ballpark mode. Line pricing is no longer required.
switched.detailed: Switched to Detailed mode. Complete pricing is available again.

mode.choosePrompt: Choose how to price this estimate. Nothing is deleted either way.
mode.ballparkTagline: Fast planning range — built from assumptions and allowances, and adjustable at any time.
mode.detailedTagline: Confirmed scope — quantities, selections and line items you price and verify.
mode.detailedHandoff: Ready for a firmer number? Build a Detailed Estimate — it keeps this scope, media, dimensions and assumptions, and the ballpark stays in history.
mode.preliminaryBody: Based on current project information and assumptions. Convert to a Detailed Estimate for a more complete scope, quantities, labor and pricing review.

convert.title: Build the Detailed Estimate from scope?
convert.body: This keeps the same estimate. Your client, property, project, title, description, notes, measurements, photos, scope, assumptions, answers and saved ballpark range are all preserved.
convert.bodyTools: Detailed pricing tools become available: quantities, labor, materials, unit pricing, line items, allowances, alternates and final pricing.
convert.bodyHistory: The original ballpark range stays in the estimate history for comparison.
convert.success: Detailed estimate built from scope. Everything was carried forward.
convert.error: We could not convert this estimate. Nothing was changed.
convert.locked: This estimate is locked, issued or archived, so it stays read-only.
convert.bandStale: This estimate now prices from its line items. The saved ballpark range is being re-checked against those lines — review any unpriced lines before sending.

pricingMode.label: Pricing
pricingMode.help: How this job is priced and presented. Switching never rebuilds the estimate — the same scope, quantities and assumptions are used every time.
pricingMode.totalHelp: One overall price or range. No labor/material breakout is shown.
pricingMode.labor_materialsHelp: Labor and material subtotals plus the combined total.
pricingMode.labor_onlyHelp: You supply labor; the owner supplies materials. Material charges are excluded from the price, but the full scope still drives the labor.

switched.total: Now pricing as one total. Scope and assumptions are unchanged.
switched.labor_materials: Now pricing as labor + materials. Scope and assumptions are unchanged.
switched.labor_only: Now pricing as labor only. Materials are excluded from the price, not from the scope.

pricingMode.excludedMaterials: Materials excluded from this price (owner supplied): {{amount}}
pricingMode.ownerSuppliedNotice: Price covers labor only. The owner supplies all materials.

financial.internalOnly: Contractor-only. Never shown on proposals, client links or PDFs.
financial.noMarkupNotice: No overhead or profit is being charged. Set defaults in estimate settings.
financial.contingencyCostNote: Contingency is counted once, as job cost, before the pricing method is applied.

financial.targetVsRealized: Target gross margin {{target}}% · realized at selected price {{realized}}%

pricingStrategy.title: Pricing method
pricingStrategy.internalOnly: Contractor-only setting. Never shown to clients.
pricingStrategy.description: Choose ONE way to price jobs. The two methods are never applied at the same time.
pricingStrategy.companyDescription: Default used by every new estimate. Any estimate can override it.
pricingStrategy.targetGrossMarginHelp: Selling price before tax = job cost ÷ (1 − target margin). Gross profit = selling price − job cost.
pricingStrategy.overheadProfitHelp: Overhead is a percentage of direct cost; profit is a percentage of direct cost + overhead.
pricingStrategy.overheadProfitGuidance: There is no universal overhead/profit pair. Set these from your actual annual overhead and sales volume: the gross margin you need is driven by your company overhead plus the net profit you want.
pricingStrategy.invalidTarget: Enter a target gross margin between 0 and 99.99%.
pricingStrategy.presetsNote: Benchmarks and published guidance — not industry standards, requirements or endorsements.

preset.gp30: 30% — near the current NAHB remodeler average benchmark
preset.gp33: 33% — full-service remodeler benchmark cited by a Qualified Remodeler contributor
preset.gp40: 40% — higher-margin remodeling guidance cited by a Qualified Remodeler contributor

pricingStrategy.sourceNahb: NAHB 2024 remodeler average (benchmark): average gross profit margin 29.9%, average net profit margin 6.3%.
pricingStrategy.sourceQr33: Qualified Remodeler contributor benchmark: successful full-service remodelers commonly cite a minimum needed gross margin of 31–33% with 7–10% net profit targets.
pricingStrategy.sourceQr40: Qualified Remodeler contributor guidance: remodelers typically need about 40% gross margin to cover overhead and earn roughly 10% net profit.
pricingStrategy.previewHint: Nothing is repriced until you save. Line costs, quantities and scope are untouched.
pricingStrategy.estimateOverride: This estimate overrides the company default.
pricingStrategy.methodDiffersNote: This estimate prices with a different method than your company default. It keeps its own method until you apply the company default here.
pricingStrategy.percentagesDifferNote: This estimate uses different percentages than your company default.
